newsitem.title: ITALY: Mother Teresa arrives in Italy needing oxygen.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa arrives in Italy needing oxygen.

text.p: Mother Teresa of Calcutta arrived in Italy on Friday for a visit and was given oxygen at Rome airport for about 20 minutes because she felt tired, a doctor said.
"It was nothing serious. She was just tired," the doctor, Giancarlo Fanti, told Reuters, after the Nobel Prize winner was taken in a wheelchair to a waiting car.

The 86-year-old nun, making her first foreign trip since she suffered serious health problems last year, blessed and smiled at reporters as she was taken to the car but did not answer questions. She was due to go to a convent run by her missionary order.

Fanti, who assisted her in a VIP lounge after her arrival, said there was no reason for alarm. "She is in good spirits," he said. Italian families adopting four Indian children who arrived with Mother Teresa were also at the airport.
The highlights of her visit to Rome are a meeting with Pope John Paul, which has not yet been scheduled, and ceremonies where some new nuns will take their vows.
Mother Teresa has said she would also like to accompany the Pope to Poland for part of his visit there next month and perhaps visit the United States if her health allowed.
